measured_first.read_from: handshake_settings, production, 2026-08-28. Configurable, not hardcoded. 22 live agreements, lifetimes 9-90 days.
measured_first.why_it_mattered: I had defended the dead-agreement publish blocker with a pick-on-Monday-publish-on-Thursday story. At 90 days that story does not hold, and the founder was right that the case is close to theoretical. His screen showing 'expires in 3 days' meant the agreement was made 87 days ago, not that he was slow.

open_question_for_founder.question: Creators pencilled into a set are held IN MEMORY ONLY — deliberately, per ledger #77, so abandoning the wizard cannot burn an agreement. So resume returns you to the right screen but does NOT restore ticks made in a previous app session.

options.A: Leave it. Resume gets you to the right place; you re-pick creators after an app restart.
options.B: Persist the picks locally so a restart keeps them. Nothing is sent to the server either way, so no agreement is actually held — the original concern was about a brand THINKING someone is committed while the agreement is free to be used elsewhere.

open_question_for_founder.answered: OPTION A — "Not surviving." Founder, 2026-08-28. Picks stay session-only. NO CODE CHANGE. Ledger #77 stands: an agreement is consumed on publish, so abandoning the wizard must not burn one, and nothing local should imply a commitment the server has never been told about.
open_question_for_founder.what_a_brand_sees: Verified rather than assumed. The SET persists on the server — name, dates, aim, channels. Only the ticks are in memory. On reopening after a restart, hydrate() reads zero creators and sends him to step 2 (Basics) with everything he typed intact; he walks forward to Creators and picks again. Nothing claims to be there that is not, and no message is possible or needed: a saved set with nobody in it is indistinguishable from a set he saved and never filled — because they are the same thing.

verification.one_real_fix_from_a_check: resumeRouteFor threw on a null campaign. Fixed in the CODE rather than softened in the test — a list that has just refreshed can hand it an undefined row for a frame, and a crash there is a blank Campaigns tab.
verification.claim: Certified no-regression. NEVER claimed green — the backend suite still cannot run.

scope_excluded: The publish gate's dead-agreement blockers — the backstop for anything already invited, which the drop never sees

release.device_walk_required: YES. W3 especially — open a set with live creators several times and confirm NOBODY disappears. The drop runs against a list that arrives asynchronously, and a guard that fails would clear a brand's work in front of them.

three_things_not_one: The only button read "+ Add another set" on a campaign with none. "Another" is a lie.

It was an OUTLINE button sitting under a BLACK "Review and publish" that was greyed out and unusable — so the one thing to do looked secondary to the thing he could not do. It is now primary while the campaign is empty.
A note explaining that a campaign may hold TWO sets showed to someone with zero. It answers a question nobody has reached yet and pushes the one action further down. Held back until there is a set.
